_doc: SASIENI dating cabinet (#11, built 2026-07-16). Dates by the SMITH SYSTEM ('Connecting the Dots', Stephen P. Smith 1996 -- THE authority, full text in our pipedia mirror staging/pipedia/Sasieni.json): nomenclature script styles + patent numbers + THE DOTS (count/size/arrangement) + town names. Eras mirror Barling's: Pre-Transition (family, 1919-1979: Joel 1919-46, Alfred 1946-79), Transition (1979-1986), Post-Transition (1986+, mid-grade). Also pipephil logo-sasieni 1+2 + sasieni-timechart (image) in mirror. Catalogs ON the pipedia page as PDFs: 1935 + 1965 + shape chart (Michael DiCuccio) -> FARID-FETCH for the catalogue inventory. ⚠️ EIGHT-DOT TRAP: the 8-dot was reissued ~1979/80 as a ~100-pc commemorative (natural, optional gold band, blue string + tab signed by Alfred) -- confirm-flow must check before dating an 8-dot to the vintage window.

history_anchors._doc: Joel Sasieni: apprenticed at CHARATAN -> DUNHILL factory manager -> own factory 1919 (burned down immediately, rebuilt; oven-cured bowls 6 weeks). Blue-dot logo -> Dunhill legal war: UK kept ONE blue dot (Europe-market until the 1960s); US: brief side-dot, then FOUR blue dots (elongated diamond) by the early-mid 1920s; by the 1930s >90% of production went to the US. EIGHT DOT debut late 1920s/early 1930s, discontinued during WWII. Joel died 1946 -> son ALFRED (nomenclature simplified, dots enlarged to equilateral diamond, patent numbers dropped, 'Four Dot' stamped -- all changes 1946-1950, then stable to 1979). 1979 sold (TRANSITION): town names eliminated, dots enlarged again, commemorative 8-dot reissue, TEN DOT with Lucite stem (Alfred quit over it -- he was vulcanite-only). 1986 sold again (POST-TRANSITION): everything a '4 Dot' (Arabic numeral), putty fills appear, 2-line nomenclature. SECONDS (own rules): Mayfair, Fantail (patent 1953), Olde English, Friar (rum-cured, rum-bottle stinger), Two Dot (= flawed four-dot quality), + the long Valitchka list (His Royal Highness, King's Court, Windsor, Barclay...). Ladies' pipes: Argyle, Montrose, Dorset. LEAD-NOT-ENCODED (BNA 2026-07-17): Worthing Herald Dec-1923 ad (image-verified, twice) sells 'The PIPE with the GREEN SPOT - THE SASIENI' at 16/6 post-free (Van Toll Bros agents) -- GREEN, not blue; single source, parked pending corroboration (see brand_research/sasieni_dating/bna_1923_green_spot_facts.md). Also: 'four dot' = zero UK newspaper hits ever -> corroborates the US-market four-dot story.

brand_marks.physical: Blue dots inserted as individual rods (like Dunhill's spot) -- originals are perfectly symmetrical; misaligned dots = replacement/fake stem. Pre-1946: SMALL dots, ELONGATED diamond + florid 'fish' script (the last i's tail sweeps under the name). Post-1946: LARGER dots, EQUILATERAL diamond, simpler script. Transition: larger still. Dots range light-to-sky blue (color varies with age -- not a dating signal).

line_years._notes: 'four dot' SPELLED OUT on shank = Alfred's 1946-50 addition, ran to the 1986 sale; '4 Dot' ARABIC NUMERAL + 2-line nomenclature = Post-Transition 1986+ (Smith: 'the easiest way to spot a Post-Transition'). TOWN NAMES (Hurlingham=apple, Grosvenor/Danzey=bulldogs, Lincoln=panel, Viscount Lascelles=large bent, Exeter=freehand-ish, Pembroke...) = introduced 1935, ELIMINATED by the new owners 1979 -> town name present = [1935,1979] HIGH-value bracket (only on Four/Eight Dot grades). fantail: seconds line, patent dated July-21-1953 -> floor 1950 approx. NOT year-encoded: the seconds list (Mayfair/Friar/Olde English/Two Dot etc. -- no documented years), ladies' lines (Argyle/Montrose/Dorset). NOTE 'grosvenor' also exists as a CHARATAN mark -- per-cabinet matching keeps them apart, but brand ID must precede.

patent_number._doc: US-market pre-WWII pipes carry patents starting '15' (150221/20, 1513428). Patents DISCONTINUED by Alfred 1946-50. EXCEPTION (Smith): some plum-finish pipes kept the patent post-war -> confidence medium, never high.

table.label: florid 'fish' script Sasieni = Joel era; Alfred dropped it immediately on taking over 1946
Eight Dot = late-1920s debut, discontinued during WWII. ⚠️ ~100-pc commemorative REISSUE 1979/80 (natural finish, blue string, signed tab, optional gold band) -> confirm before dating vintage
Ten Dot with Lucite stem = Transition firm only (the line that made Alfred quit)
One Dot = Europe-market until the 1960s (US one-dots = 1919-c.1925 only; side-dot = ultra-rare early-20s -> confirm-flow)
small dots in elongated diamond = pre-Alfred-enlargement

stamped_year._doc: Generic channel. Sasieni rarely stamps years; commemoratives may.

channels_future.catalogues: 1935 + 1965 catalog PDFs + shape chart PDF are LINKED on the pipedia Sasieni page (DiCuccio) -> FARID-FETCH; enables shape brackets (by 1935: 50 shapes) + XS/S-suffix decoding (XS = premium shape all grades, XS* = premium in 4-Dot only; trailing s = saddle variant where a tapered twin exists).
